System design

Two facades:

  1. Frontoffice ("Al-Moushir" / المستشار — the assistant): public/customer-facing chat, trilingual, embedded widget on albaraka.com.tn + standalone web app + optionally mobile. Anonymous + authenticated customers. No access to core banking data in v1 (only public KB: products, Sharia concepts, fees, agency locator, procedures). Later phases: authenticated account queries via core banking adapter (with strict scoping).
  2. Backoffice: admin console for KB editors, Sharia officers, ML/AI engineers, compliance, support agents. Modules: Knowledge Base, Prompt Studio, Retrieval Lab, Sharia Review Board workflow, Model & Provider config, Guardrails policy, Feedback & QA loop, Analytics, Users & roles (via Keycloak), Audit.

Backend (Spring Boot 4 + Spring AI 2.0) — modular monolith with clean module boundaries (hexagonal per module):

  • assistant-api (chat orchestration, SSE streaming)
  • rag-core (retrieval pipeline: query understanding → rewrite → hybrid retrieve → rerank → context assembly)
  • knowledge (documents, chunks, versions, embeddings lifecycle)
  • ingestion (connectors, parsing, chunking, translation, embedding jobs)
  • governance (Sharia review workflow, approvals, content lifecycle states, audit)
  • guardrails (input/output moderation, prompt injection, haram-topic policy, PII redaction)
  • identity (Keycloak resource server, role/claims mapping)
  • analytics (metrics, feedback, cost/token accounting)
  • admin-api (backoffice REST)
  • audit (immutable append-only log, hash-chained)

RAG pipeline detail: Query → language detect (fastText/CLD3 or LLM) → intent classify (product_question, sharia_ruling, procedural, account_status, out_of_scope, greeting, adversarial) → guardrail pre-check (Llama Guard 4 + Prompt Guard 2 + custom haram-topic classifier) → query rewriting/expansion:

  • trilingual query expansion: generate FR/AR/EN variants + Arabic normalization (remove diacritics/tashkeel, Alef variants أإآ→ا, ة→ه, ى→ي, tatweel removal) + Tunisian dialect → MSA mapping (e.g. "نحب ناخذ قرض" → "أرغب في الحصول على تمويل"; "باش" "شنية" "برشة")
    • HyDE optional → Retrieval: hybrid
    • dense: pgvector HNSW cosine on halfvec(1536) with metadata filter (language, audience, product, status=PUBLISHED, valid_at, sharia_approved=true)
    • sparse/keyword: Postgres FTS. Key issue: Postgres FTS has no built-in Arabic or French stemmer for Arabic; French can use unaccent + french text search config; Arabic needs a custom text search configuration (e.g., using pg_arabic/rum or ICU tokenizer + a custom Arabic stemmer via extension, or app-side Light Stemmer (Tashaphyne) writing stemmed tokens into a tsvector column). Decision: do app-side normalization+light stemming and store a generated tsvector via to_tsvector('simple', normalized_tokens) — robust and no exotic extension. Plus keep trigram index (pg_trgm) for typo tolerance.
    • cross-lingual: because gemini-embedding-001 is multilingual, an Arabic query can retrieve French documents (cross-lingual dense). Also store per-chunk translations (canonical source + FR/AR/EN renderings) and retrieve on all, but generate in the user's language.
    • RRF fusion (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) → rerank. Reranker: no native Groq/Google reranker; options: (a) LLM-based listwise rerank via Groq llama-3.1-8b-instant (cheap, fast) with structured JSON output, (b) cross-encoder served on-prem (e.g., bge-reranker-v2-m3 via a small Python sidecar/ONNX in Java). Decision: ADR — v1 uses LLM rerank via Groq (cheap model, batched, cached), v2 introduces an on-prem cross-encoder sidecar for cost/latency/compliance. Document both. → Context assembly with per-chunk citation ids, token budget (context window management, e.g. 8k budget), dedup, ordering, provenance metadata. → Generation: Groq llama-3.3-70b-versatile (or gpt-oss-120b) with streaming SSE, response contract: answer + inline citations [S1], sources array, confidence, "no-answer" behaviour, mandatory disclaimers (not a fatwa; refer to comité chariaa), refusal templates. → Post-generation guardrails: citation grounding check (every claim maps to a retrieved chunk), Sharia policy classifier on the output (detect riba/interest-rate promises, haram product endorsement, unapproved fatwa issuance), numeric/financial-claim validation, PII redaction, banned-phrase filter, language consistency check. → Persist: conversation, message, retrieval trace (candidates + scores), token usage, feedback hooks.

Sharia governance (the differentiator): Content lifecycle: DRAFT → IN_REVIEW → SHARIA_APPROVED → PUBLISHED → DEPRECATED → RETIRED. Every chunk inherits document state; only SHARIA_APPROVED+PUBLISHED chunks are retrievable by the frontoffice. Backoffice-only retrieval can include IN_REVIEW (flagged). Roles: KB_EDITOR, SHARIA_OFFICER (member of comité de contrôle de conformité des normes bancaires islamiques per Art. 54 loi 2016-48), SHARIA_AUDITOR (auditeur des opérations bancaires islamiques per circulaire BCT 2021-05), COMPLIANCE, AI_ENGINEER, ADMIN, AGENT, CUSTOMER. Key rule: the assistant never issues a fatwa. It can only relay published, approved content and must attach the standing disclaimer + route "is X halal?" ruling requests to the Sharia committee via a ticket (fatwa request workflow). Two-eyes principle: any change to system prompts, guardrail policy, or KB content requires a second approver; prompt changes touching Sharia phrasing require SHARIA_OFFICER approval. All changes hash-chained in audit log; monthly/annual report export (the comité's annual report to the CA/AGO — RGA240220 per BCT reporting) can include AI-assistant Sharia conformity annex. Also: "Nafaa al Am"/charity account irrelevant here. Skip. Prohibited-content policy: no interest/riba promotion, no conventional-loan comparison advice, no gambling/maysir, no financing of haram sectors (alcohol, pork, weapons?, tobacco, adult content), no takfir/sectarian content, no political/sectarian religious rulings, no personal religious counseling beyond bank products.

Trilingual specifics:

  • Locale negotiation: Accept-Language, user profile, URL prefix /fr|/ar|/en, widget param.
  • AR: RTL layout (dir="rtl"), bidi handling in mixed content (account numbers, amounts, Latin product names) → use <bdi>, CSS logical properties, Angular CDK BidiModule. Arabic fonts (Noto Naskh Arabic / IBM Plex Sans Arabic / Cairo), digit choice (Western Arabic 0-9 vs Eastern Arabic ٠١٢٣) → configurable, default Western for Tunisia (Tunisia uses 0-9 typically).
  • Currency: TND formatting, Intl.NumberFormat('ar-TN').
  • Answer language policy: always answer in the language of the question (detect), regardless of source doc language; keep technical terms with transliteration on first use: "Mourabaha (المرابحة)".
  • Glossary-driven terminology consistency: canonical term table (fr/ar/en + definition + approved translations) injected into prompts to prevent mistranslation of Sharia terms (e.g., don't translate "Mourabaha" as "prêt"/"loan"; avoid "intérêt" → use "marge bénéficiaire" / "هامش ربح").
  • Tunisian Derja handling: normalizer maps Derja → MSA for retrieval; answer in MSA (professional) — never invent Derja fatwas.
  • i18n mechanism: Angular @angular/localize vs runtime translation service. Decision: runtime i18n with JSON dictionaries (needed since backoffice admins edit UI copy? maybe not) — but for a bank, AOT compile-time i18n is standard. Trade-off: 3 locales × 2 apps = 6 builds with @angular/localize; or runtime loader for flexibility. ADR: runtime loader with lazy per-locale JSON + AOT fallback, because we need dynamic language switching without reload and RTL flip, plus admin-editable microcopy later.

Security & compliance (Tunisia):

  • Keycloak OIDC: two clients (albaraka-assistant-web public PKCE for frontoffice, albaraka-backoffice-web public PKCE + step-up/MFA for admins), realm roles → Spring @PreAuthorize. Backend = OAuth2 resource server (JWT). Service-to-service: client credentials.
  • Data protection: Loi organique n° 2004-63 (INPDP declaration), Loi 2018-32? Also Loi n° 2004-63 du 27 juillet 2004 relative à la protection des données à caractère personnel. Banking secrecy: Art. 79-83 loi 2016-48 (secret professionnel). Data residency: personal data must not leave Tunisia without INPDP authorization → critical architectural consequence: sending customer data to Groq (US) / Google (US) is a compliance risk. Mitigation: (1) v1 = public, non-personal KB only → no personal data sent to LLM providers; (2) PII detection + redaction/tokenization before any external API call; (3) DPA + contractual guarantees; (4) roadmap: on-prem inference (vLLM/Ollama) as an alternative profile (that's why pluggable adapter). Also BCT circular on outsourcing/cloud (Circulaire BCT n° 2018-10? or 2020-05 on "les règles de bonne conduite"?) — I should be careful citing specific circular numbers I'm unsure of. I'll cite the ones I verified: Loi 2016-48 (arts. 22, 53/54 comité, 58 audit, 69 systémique, 100-102), Circulaire BCT n° 2021-05 du 19 août 2021 (gouvernance, incl. ch. on Islamic banking ops, art. 56, 58, 59, 65), AAOIFI Sharia standards, and for data: Loi organique 2004-63 + INPDP; and note "BCT outsourcing/cloud circular — to be confirmed with Compliance" as an open item rather than inventing a number. Good: flag verification-needed items explicitly. That's honest and professional.
  • Prompt injection defense: Prompt Guard 2 + system-prompt isolation + no tool access to sensitive APIs in v1 + strict output schema + rate limiting + per-IP throttling.
  • Audit: append-only, hash-chained, WORM-ish, 10y retention for banking.
  • Secrets: Vault or Spring Cloud Vault / K8s secrets + env; never in DB plaintext; admin-configured provider keys encrypted with AES-GCM + KMS envelope.

Observability & eval:

  • OTel traces across retrieve→rerank→generate (span per stage, token counts, costs), Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboards, Loki logs (with PII scrubbing), alerting on refusal-rate spikes, Sharia-flag rate, latency P95 < 3s (Groq is fast).
  • Eval harness: golden set (trilingual QA pairs with expected citations + expected refusal), RAGAS-style metrics (faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision/recall), plus Sharia-specific eval: policy-violation rate, disclaimer presence, haram-topic refusal correctness, terminology accuracy vs glossary, hallucinated product/fee detection. CI gate: no prompt/model/KB change ships without eval run passing thresholds. Shadow/canary deployment with A/B on prompt versions.
  • Human feedback loop: 👍/👎 + reason codes + "report a Sharia concern" button → triage queue → KB fix or prompt fix → regression test added to golden set.

Data model (Postgres): Tables: document, document_version, chunk, chunk_embedding (halfvec), chunk_translation, term_glossary, collection/knowledge_source, ingestion_job, conversation, message, retrieval_trace, retrieval_candidate, feedback, sharia_review (workflow instance), review_task, prompt_template, prompt_version, deployment_config (model config versions), guardrail_policy, guardrail_event, audit_event, user_profile(locale prefs), fatwa_request, api_token_budget, eval_run, eval_case_result, ab_experiment, analytics_daily. I need to be careful: searchable as a generated column can't reference other tables, so it must be computed from columns on chunk — I'll keep sharia_approved, published, valid_from, valid_to denormalized onto chunk (maintained by trigger) and make searchable a STORED generated column from those. That's clean and gives a real DB-level guarantee.

Let me design chunk columns: published boolean, sharia_approved boolean, valid_from, valid_to, audience, and searchable boolean GENERATED ALWAYS AS (published AND sharia_approved AND coalesce(valid_from, '-infinity') <= now() ...) STORED — problem: now() is not immutable, so it can't be used in a generated column. Right. So instead: searchable is a real column maintained by a trigger on write + a scheduled job that flips expiry (e.g., a pg_cron-ish job or app scheduler running every minute: UPDATE chunk SET searchable=false WHERE valid_to < now() AND searchable). I'll document that. And retrieval additionally checks valid_to for belt-and-braces.

So: searchable boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false maintained by trigger fn_recompute_chunk_searchable() on insert/update of the relevant columns, plus a periodic expiry sweeper. Document it.

tsv: tsv tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('albaraka_fts', coalesce(normalized_text,''))) STORED — to_tsvector with a config name literal is immutable, so this works as a generated column. Good (the two-argument form with a regconfig constant is immutable; to_tsvector(text) without config is not).

Audit hash chain: trigger on insert computing hash = sha256(prev_hash || canonical json). Use encode(digest(...,'sha256'),'hex') from pgcrypto.

Self-approval trigger: on review_task insert/update, check that assignee_id <> (select submitted_by from sharia_review where id = review_id).

T3 quorum: deferred constraint trigger on sharia_review update to APPROVED requiring tasks with both roles.

Contents for each utility prompt:

INTENT_CLASSIFIER (model_role CHAT_FAST, llama-3.1-8b-instant)

Input: normalized user text + last 2 turns. Output JSON: intent (14), language (fr-FR/ar-TN/en-GB), dialect_detected, sharia_sensitive, needs_disclaimer, pii_hint, confidence. Rules: single label; precedence ADVERSARIAL > ABUSE > OUT_OF_SCOPE > ... etc. Include the precedence ladder and per-intent definitions + few-shot examples trilingual.

QUERY_REWRITE (CHAT_FAST)

Input: question + history + glossary + detected intent. Output JSON: primary_query, variants[], expansions (glossary-only), translated_query (cross-lingual fallback), search_hints. Rules: no invented terms, glossary-only expansion, preserve numbers verbatim, ≤ 4 variants, arabizi→MSA.

SYSTEM_RERANKER (RERANKER, CHAT_FAST)

Listwise rerank of up to 40 candidates → top 12 with relevance score 0-1 and reason code. Output JSON array of {id, score, reason}. Reason enum: DIRECT_ANSWER, PARTIAL, DEFINITION, PROCEDURE, TARIFF, RELATED, IRRELEVANT, OUTDATED. Strict: id must be from input list, no duplicates, order descending.

ANSWER_CONTRACT

That's now FALSE — the verb won, and the waqf entry (وقف = endowment) is in the sharia category... wait, sharia list has ("وقف","waqf","وقف","endowment",0.98) but it came later so was skipped. So the map now says وقف → أوقف (he stopped), losing the endowment sense. That's a real quality problem for an Islamic bank: وقف/waqf is domain-critical!
  • صغير: adjective "small" (0.98) won over noun "small/young" (0.95) — fine.
  • مضمون: noun "municipal extract" (0.90) won over adjective "guaranteed" (0.85) — acceptable, note says so.

So I must fix وقف: remove the verb entry (or rename it to a distinct surface form) so the endowment sense survives. In Derja, "to stop" as a transitive verb is usually وقّف (wa99ef) with shadda on the ف — spelled وقّف. And the noun وقف (waqf) is the endowment. Using the shadda distinguishes them in writing: وقّف vs وقف. That's linguistically accurate too: Derja Form II وقّف "he stopped (something)".

So: change the verb entry to ("وقّف","wa99ef","أوقف","he stopped (something)",0.80) and keep sharia وقف → وقف endowment at 0.98. Both unique.

Similarly check for other silent semantic losses among the skipped dupes — only those 4. Good.

Check (g) is valuable: e.g. ("نصف","noss","نصف",...) where derja == msa is a no-op mapping; ("حساب","حساب") no-op; ("دين","دين") no-op. No-op mappings are harmless but noise; better: flag when derjaAr == msa (identity mapping) — should be removed or justified. These are cases where the Derja form IS the MSA form. They're useless as mappings (identity), but they DO carry a purpose: they mark the term as "known Derja/MSA-shared", preventing the admin mining screen from proposing them. Hmm. But for the DB they're pure noise and would double-map nothing.

Decision: keep them but flag as identity: true with a note that they are retained as "known-shared vocabulary" to suppress mining proposals? That's a legitimate design, but it inflates the row count with no-ops and complicates the seed. That's honest data modelling: a mapping table shouldn't contain non-mappings.

The collision reporting worked — exactly the lesson from وقف. Now:

  1. جاب collision: verb "he brought" (→ أحضر) vs finance "GAB" (ATM, → موزع آلي). Both are written جاب in Arabic script! That's a genuine homograph. The ATM sense is usually written جاب or "GAB" in latin. Resolution: keep the verb (much more frequent), and for the ATM use a distinct surface form: "جاب الآلي" or write it as the latin-only "GAB"... but derja_ar is NOT NULL and unique, so a latin-only entry needs an Arabic-script form. Options: "موزع آلي جاب"? Better: use "الجاب" (el-GAB, with the definite article) which is how Tunisians actually say it ("نمشي للجاب"). That's a distinct string and natural. Let me use "الجاب" → "الموزع الآلي".

  2. شهرية duplicate: same target, just listed twice in two categories. Harmless — dedupe handled it. But I should remove the redundant entry from the adverb list (it was a stray). Actually the adverb one is a mistake in my authoring (I appended a bunch of finance/adjective identity entries under "adverb"). Those went to sharedVocabulary mostly. The شهرية in adverb was a non-identity duplicate → dropped. Fine. But it reveals my category tagging for that big tail block is wrong (finance terms tagged "adverb"). Let me fix the categories for the tail block: I put a huge list of finance/adjective/adverb identity entries under grp("adverb", ...). Those with identity go to sharedVocabulary with category "adverb" — mislabeled.

Since sharedVocabulary is authoring metadata only (not seeded), mislabeled category is a data-quality issue worth fixing. Let me re-tag: move the clearly-finance items to "finance" and adjectives to "adjective". That's a chunk of editing.

Simpler and cleaner: introduce a per-row category correction by splitting that tail grp("adverb", ...) into three groups: adverb (real adverbs/prepositions/numerals), finance (banking nouns), adjective (descriptors). Let me restructure that tail properly.

  1. "present in both lists": حل, عام, قريب — mapping wins, shared entry dropped. For حل: noun "solution" is identity (حل→حل) and the verb حلّ (with shadda) is a mapping. Wait — I wrote the verb as "حل" without shadda in the verb group: ("حل","7all","فتح",...) — so derjaAr "حل" appears both as verb→فتح (mapping) and noun→حل (shared). Collision resolved in favour of the mapping, which loses the noun "solution" from sharedVocabulary. That's the same trap as وقف! Fix: write the verb with shadda "حلّ" (U+0651) to disambiguate, matching what I did for وقّف. Then noun حل stays in sharedVocabulary and verb حلّ is a mapping.

Same for عام: adjective "general" (عام→عام identity) vs "year" (عام→سنة mapping). Both strings identical! Genuine homograph — can't disambiguate orthographically. Resolution: the mapping (→ سنة) wins, and the adjective sense is recorded in an ambiguity note rather than as a separate row. I have a note field available. Let me add a note to the عام mapping explaining the two senses and that the year reading dominates in banking chat ("عام" in a duration question).

Hmm, but that means "القطاع العام" would map to "القطاع سنة" — catastrophic! Word-boundary mapping with longest-match-first would replace عام → سنة inside القطاع العام. That's a real hazard. Better: LOWER confidence and require context. Since the map is applied mechanically, a homograph that can produce nonsense must NOT be in the map at all. Correct resolution: remove عام→سنة from the mappings and put it in sharedVocabulary as عام→عام with a note that the "year" sense is handled by context (and the surface form is identical in MSA anyway — عام IS valid MSA for "year"!). Indeed: عام is standard MSA for year. So there's nothing to map. Drop the mapping entirely, keep as shared.

Same logic applies to قريب: adjective "near" (قريب is valid MSA) vs adverb "almost". The adverbial mapping قريب→تقريبا is dangerous (a "near branch" question would become "almost branch"). Remove from mappings; قريب is valid MSA, put in sharedVocabulary with a note.

Same check for other risky homographs I included:

  • كان → إذا: كان is also MSA "was". Mapping كان→إذا mechanically would destroy "كان البنك مفتوحا" → "إذا البنك مفتوحا". DANGEROUS. But Derja uses كان for "if" very commonly... Still, mechanical replacement is unsafe. Resolution: keep with a note and confidence 0.85, BUT the map is applied with word boundaries and longest-match-first — that doesn't fix homography. The honest answer: homographs where both senses are frequent must be handled by the intent/context layer, not by a blind string map. I'll keep كان but lower to 0.70 with an explicit note that it is applied only when no finite verb follows... Actually the map can't express that.

Let me adopt a principled rule and encode it in the JSON: homographPolicy — entries whose MSA target would be ungrammatical in the other sense are marked "contextRequired": true and the linter asserts every such entry has a note AND confidence ≤ 0.80. The runtime applies contextRequired entries only when the surrounding query matches a cheap contextual predicate recorded in contextWhen (e.g. "no finite verb follows", "query is a duration question"). That's honest engineering: it makes the limitation explicit and testable rather than hiding it in a confidence float.

Entries needing contextRequired: كان (if/was), دين (debt/religion), جمعة (week/Friday), قريب (almost/near — I'll move to shared), توظيف (investment/recruitment), معلوم (fee/known), أداء (tax/performance), معارضة (stop-payment/opposition), بوليصة (policy/document), حوش (house/courtyard), عدى (crossed/passed), بيت (room/house-of?), ما زال, ماشي, خلاص, حل (fixed via shadda), عام (fixed → shared), وكالة (shared), وقف (fixed), ضمان (shared), حساب (shared).

What the new linter caught

tools/i18n-lint is finished: 24 check groups, 0 errors, 5 advisory warnings, 77-mutation self-test. Its expectations are derived from four authorities (schema.sql, docs/03 §8, docs/06 §7, specs/config/application.yaml), and the self-test mutates copies of those authorities too — that's the proof it reads them rather than copying them.

First run produced 10 errors, all real. The significant one:

The dialect map ran after the stemmer. A key the stemmer alters can never match — and worse, it can land on a different key:

text
معلومات → (stem) → معلوم   which is itself an entry meaning "fee"
                            so "information" was rewritten as "fee"
الجاب   → (stem) → جاب     ("he brought") so "the ATM" became "he brought"
إجراءات، عمليات، اليوم، البنك  all lose an affix and become unreachable

Nothing errors. The mapping just stops happening, and it presents as weak recall — someone would have concluded the embeddings were bad. stageOrder is now fold → dialect_map → stem, with the counterexamples written into docs/03 §8 and asserted by check N13.

Also fixed: آش → ما → لا (a chain that turned "what" into "not"), تولد → ولد → ابن ("was born" → "son"), and ما → لا / يعمل → يفعل, which were valid MSA and corrupted MSA queries — the map is now gated on Derja detection (policy.appliesWhen), with every removal recorded in prunedEntries so nobody re-adds it. And appliesTo claimed a column document_version.normalized_text that doesn't exist — normalised text lives on chunk only, which is what keeps approved content from having a second rewritable copy.

The self-test paid for itself immediately: deleting a NOT NULL column made a downstream loop throw, so the process died with a stack trace where CI expected findings. A crashed linter is worse than an incomplete one — malformed rows are now skipped by every later loop, and an unexpected throw prints INTERNAL and exits 2.

Hmm. Which is more defensible? Actually the cleanest and most conventional Spring Boot + Flyway design:

  • Flyway migrations seed content (deterministic, versioned, reviewed, idempotent).
  • YAML holds only environment wiring + secrets + values that legitimately differ per environment.
  • If a value must differ per environment (e.g. budget, provider keys), it's YAML/env.

The albaraka.seed block in YAML duplicates what Flyway should own. That's a genuine architectural smell I introduced earlier. But changing it now means touching specs/config (and config-lint's 103 checks derive from it).

Alternative resolution that keeps both coherent: YAML albaraka.seed is the input; V902 is generated from it. I.e., the seed migrations are generated artefacts from the YAML + spec files, and a lint check verifies they agree. That preserves "single source of truth" (the YAML/spec files are authored; the SQL is generated) and gives Flyway deterministic versioned content.

That's actually elegant and matches what docs/glossary-trilingual.md already says: "the seed migration V900__seed_glossary.sql is generated from it". And specs/prompts/templates.refusals.yaml says it's the "Source of truth for the message_bundle rows seeded by V902". So the repository's own docs already establish: docs/spec files are authored sources of truth; the V9xx SQL is generated from them.

js
const SEED_NAMESPACE = 'a1ba4a4a-0000-5000-8000-000000000000';function uuidBytes(u){ return Buffer.from(u.replace(/-/g,''),'hex'); }export function uuidv5(name, ns=SEED_NAMESPACE){  const h = createHash('sha1').update(Buffer.concat([uuidBytes(ns), Buffer.from(name,'utf8')])).digest();  const b = Buffer.from(h.subarray(0,16));  b[6] = (b[6] & 0x0f) | 0x50;   // version 5  b[8] = (b[8] & 0x3f) | 0x80;   // variant  const s = b.toString('hex');  return `${s.slice(0,8)}-${s.slice(8,12)}-${s.slice(12,16)}-${s.slice(16,20)}-${s.slice(20)}`;}

G6d failed — that's a real finding. Let me see which placeholders are undeclared:

Not a data finding — a SQL bug in my test. LATERAL regexp_matches(v.body, '\{\{(\w+)\}\}', 'g') AS p(var) — the issue is that the regex \{\{(\w+)\}\} inside a standard string literal: PostgreSQL with standard_conforming_strings=on treats backslashes literally, so the regex is fine.

The error "malformed array literal: "}}"" suggests p.var isn't what I think — actually regexp_matches returns text[], and I aliased it as p(var) so var should be the array's... no! regexp_matches returns a SET OF text[] — one row per match, each row being an array of capture groups. When I write AS p(var), I'm naming the single column var, which is a text[] (the array of capture groups), not a text. So p.var = ANY(v.variables) compares text[] to text → and the error comes from trying to interpret... hmm, "malformed array literal: "}}"".

Fix: use p(var)[1] — subscript the capture-group array. So:

sql
FROM prompt_version v, LATERAL regexp_matches(v.body, '\{\{(\w+)\}\}', 'g') AS p(m)WHERE NOT (p.m[1] = ANY (v.variables))

And in the string_agg use p.m[1].

The problem: string_agg(c, ', ') where c comes from a subquery containing SRFs — PG complains the aggregate contains a set-returning call. Fix: wrap with explicit subselects that materialise:

sql
WITH seeded AS (SELECT DISTINCT split_part(message_key,'.',2) AS c FROM message_bundle WHERE message_key LIKE 'refusal.%'),     policy AS (SELECT jsonb_object_keys(value) AS c FROM assistant_config WHERE key='refusal.policy')SELECT string_agg(c, ', ') INTO bad FROM (  (SELECT c FROM seeded EXCEPT SELECT c FROM policy)  UNION ALL  (SELECT c FROM policy EXCEPT SELECT c FROM seeded)) x;
